sentences.text:
This is an application for anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
filed by the sole accused in Crime No.1345 of 2023 of Petta Police Station, Thiruvananthapuram District, registered under Sections 376, 354A(i)(ii), 506 and 509 of IPC.

2. The prosecution allegation is that on 05.12.2022, the petitioner sexually assaulted the victim and forcibly subjected her to oral sex, promising to marry her.
3. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor.
4. Learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application, stating that presence of the petitioner is necessary for conducting potency test.
5.
Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the victim lady stated before the Doctor that she was in a romantic relationship with the petitioner for two years.
The petitioner is a Medical Doctor, doing his post-graduation in AIMS, Raipur.
The defacto complainant is also a Doctor, who was senior to him, while they were studying at Medical College, Alappuzha.

The allegation by the defacto complainant that the petitioner compelled her to have oral sex with her in broad daylight,
that too inside the car, is not liable to be believed according to him, and he produced Annexure-2 copy of the complaint dated 26.11.2023 preferred by the petitioner herein before the City Police Commissioner, Thiruvananthapuram, alleging that the defacto complainant herein is spreading false news against him in Social Media and she is posting defamatory messages in the official facebook page of the Cosmopolitan Hospitals Pvt. Ltd., where his father is working as a Neurologist.
The defacto complainant lodged First Information Statement before Police on 03.12.2023, i.e., after filing Annexure-2 complaint by the petitioner before the City Police Commissioner.
Moreover, the report of the Medico-Legal Examination of the survivor would show that the defacto complainant refused for medical examination.
6. In this factual scenario, this Court is inclined to allow this application on the following terms:
( i ) The petitioner shall appear before the investigating officer on 29.01.2024 at 10.00 a.m., and subject himself for interrogation.
The investigating officer can interrogate him and collect all materials and evidence within the reach of the petitioner, which are found necessary for the investigation.

(ii) In the event of arrest, he shall be released on bail on executing bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the arresting officer.
(iii) Thereafter, the petitioner shall appear before the investigating officer as and when directed to do so.

(iv) The petitioner shall not enter the limits of Petta Police Station, Thiruvananthapuram, except for the purpose of reporting before the Police Station and for appearing before the court, as and when Amir S vs State Of Kerala on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115985135/
2 directed.
(v) The petitioner shall not try to contact, influence or intimidate the victim or her family members,
either directly or indirectly.
(vi) The petitioner shall not leave the limits of India without getting prior sanction from the trial court.
(vii) The petitioner shall not commit any offence while on bail.
